A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same EMMA benchmark. All 24 pages of each version, including appendices, are readable, and corresponding text, equations, tables and figures can be matched despite relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: Section 4 and Table 3 report original evaluations of five concept-erasure methods across five domains. The appendices include classifier comparisons, bias analyses and generated-image examples.

after.justification: V2 retains the original benchmark experiments and adds human prompt-identification results in Table 5 and computational profiling results in Table 7.

M1.justification: The model backbones, erasure procedures, concept mappings, prompt construction and classifier pipeline are retained. Method descriptions in v1 Section 7.3 match v2 Appendix B.3; the additions concern evaluation and documentation.

E1.justification: Appendix A.3 adds a human task of identifying concepts from indirect descriptions. The image-generation benchmark retains the same 206 concepts across objects, celebrities, art styles, NSFW and copyright, with unchanged explicit/implicit and random/similar scenarios.

E2.justification: Both versions evaluate CA, ESD, UCE, MACE and FMN against the same Stable Diffusion models. Classifier and image-similarity comparators also remain unchanged. PGCE, SEE and EraseBench receive additional literature coverage, not new experimental comparisons.

E3.justification: V2 adds hardware-independent compute-budget evaluation and a five-choice human study involving 94 prompts and four native English speakers. Existing image-generation settings remain unchanged; newly disclosed training-iteration counts do not establish changes to the original training protocol.

E4.justification: Appendix A.3 tests whether indirect prompts identify their intended concepts for humans. Appendix B.1 adds computational profiling to examine operation counts alongside wall-clock latency. Existing classifier validation, bias case studies and qualitative analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Random-seed descriptions remain unchanged, and neither version reports confidence intervals, significance tests or run-to-run uncertainty. The new human study reports accuracy without uncertainty estimates or inter-annotator agreement.

E6.justification: V2 Table 5 adds overall human identification accuracies of 0.91 for short descriptions and 0.93 for long descriptions; Table 7 adds computational-cost results. Main Table 3, classifier results in v1 Table 6/v2 Table 8, and SSIM results in v1 Table 7/v2 Table 9 are numerically unchanged.

T1.justification: The EA, RA, bias and Jaccard definitions retain their meaning. EA/RA equations become inline, the bias equation is renumbered, and the standard FID formula is omitted as explanatory compression. No substantive theoretical assumptions, derivations or proofs change.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction expand the claimed benchmark coverage from 12 to 13 metrics by adding compute budget. The central claims about incomplete implicit erasure, impaired retention of similar concepts and possible bias amplification remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 explains latency differences through implementation overhead, qualifies demographic reference groups, suggests an association between training iterations and bias shifts, and adds specific future directions. It removes v1's limitations concerning within-task retention comparisons and unresolved causes of bias amplification.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-and-prompts repository link. Appendix B.1 newly documents end-to-end timing on Name prompts, CalFLOPs profiling, parameter and iteration counts, external-data requirements and pipeline characteristics. These disclosures do not establish that existing implementations changed.

R1.justification: V2 adds PGCE and SEE citations and expands discussion of the already-cited EraseBench. Section 2 replaces the blanket assertion that prior benchmarks lack challenging assessments with more specific distinctions about hierarchical coverage and long descriptions. The Inception reference is removed alongside the FID formula.

P1.justification: V2 locally rewrites related work and the conclusion, compresses metric explanations, adds a supplementary-material roadmap, and relabels appendices 6–9 as A–D. Terminology, grammar and acknowledgments receive limited edits; the overall narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds human-evaluation and compute-budget tables and expands Table 1 with a Compute column and PGCE, EraseBench and SEE rows. Existing tables and figures are relocated or renumbered, including the SSIM table; the original figure imagery is retained.

improvement.justification: Human prompt validation in Table 5 strengthens the benchmark's semantic grounding, while compute profiling in Table 7 makes timing results more interpretable. Added reproducibility information and more qualified research positioning provide further limited gains. These benefits are tempered by removing explicit limitations and suggesting an iteration–bias explanation without a controlled test; the core benchmark results remain unchanged.
